correctness.rationale: At t=0 all mixed faces are crossing edges between two full shore simplices, yielding ab−1 circles. For t>=1 direct induced-degree case split gives two shore simplices, hub cone u*(simplex B0 * discrete B1), mixed edges and unique triangles (u,x,z) for x∈A\{u}, z∈faulted B0. Each edge {x,z} has only that triangle coface, giving (a−1)t legal elementary collapses. The remainder is a contractible connected core (gluing along nonempty contractible intersections) plus precisely (a−1)(b−t) extra one-cells, with integral cycle basis c_{x,y}. These cycles existed in earlier stages and the new triangles kill only specified basis elements, proving split surjection and primitive kernels. Independently direct induced-degree enumeration for (a,b)=(3,4),(4,4) at all 0<=t<=b recovered the explicit face families. Mod-2 tests do not replace CW proof.
